what: Macerich is a REIT that owns shopping malls, concentrated in dense, affluent markets in California, Arizona, the New York metropolitan area and a handful of other states. It is in the middle of a plan to sell weaker properties and reinvest in its best ones.
customers: Retailers leasing mall space, from department stores and national chains to restaurants, entertainment operators and increasingly medical and office tenants filling former retail space.
money: Base rent plus rent tied to tenant sales volumes.
Reimbursement of operating costs, plus parking, advertising and management fees.
moat: Its better malls sit in densely populated, high-income catchment areas where no new mall will ever be built, and for many retailers a physical presence in those specific centres still drives sales. Redeveloping surplus department store space into apartments, offices or entertainment uses adds value no newcomer could create.
risks: Debt of about $5.1B against a $6.7B market value and $280.2M of cash is the central problem; the equity sits behind a very large borrowing load.
The trailing period shows a net loss of about $98.9M, and free cash flow of $33.7M is minimal.
Mall retail faces structural decline in the United States, and anchor department stores continue to shrink.
Selling weak malls in a market with few buyers for weak malls takes time and realises low prices.
The shares trade at about 20.1 times EV/EBITDA and 198 times free cash flow, which reflects how little cash the portfolio currently throws off.
opportunities: Revenue has grown each year shown, from $847.4M in 2021 to $1.0B in 2025, as occupancy and rents at the better centres recovered.
The strategy of concentrating on the strongest malls and giving back the weakest is the right response to the structural problem, and it is measurable.
Redeveloping former department store boxes into housing or mixed use unlocks value that mall accounting does not reflect.
Fifteen analysts average a $26.87 target, about 14% above the current price.
watch: Leased occupancy and releasing spreads at the retained malls. The disposal plan only works if the kept properties are genuinely healthy, and those two figures are where that shows.
